description: One-person team from the University of Windsor analysing long-term trends in NASA Earth observation data.
summary: TrendScope is a concept and analysis design for detecting statistically significant long-term trends in NASA Earth system variables. Using NASA POWER temperature, precipitation and solar irradiance records, it answers four questions for any location: what is changing, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant. It combines the non-parametric Mann-Kendall test with the Theil-Sen slope estimator and corrects for autocorrelation and multiple testing, so that users see only trends that survive rigorous checks.
details: TrendScope is a methodology and design concept that detects statistically significant trends in NASA POWER climate data using the Mann-Kendall test and the Theil-Sen slope, with corrections for autocorrelation and multiple testing. A working prototype was not completed. Planned tools: Python, NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib.
